t: Hand-painted, and repainted: perennial flowers and bulbs, installation and maintenance — and, underneath, Kate Butler, handweaver, fine woollens and more. Two trades on one signpost.
An 1800s Greek Revival, restored room by room. Inside: the antiques, craft and gift shop, and three guest rooms full of tropical plants that have no business being this far north.
Not a sales yard — a garden. Alpine miniatures at your feet, background giants behind them, and the whole point being to show you what a Zone-3 border can actually look like in August.
English cottage planting on one side, formal display on the other. The same plants, arranged two ways, so you can see which argument you find more persuasive.
Field-grown or potted, your choice. Everything here was raised from seed or by division on this ground — which is why it survives the winter after you take it home.
Where the oddball stuff lives. Alpines, creepers, and a running experiment in what is genuinely not supposed to do well up here.
Among the flowers and along the water. Bring lunch, stay the afternoon; nobody will hurry you toward the till.
The Barton River runs the length of the property. Moisture-lovers get the bank, and the sound of it carries right up into the gardens.
